# Creating Demand In a Digital Era

Global industry leader Procter & Gamble faced the consequences after being unable to effectively implement marketing strategies to stay competitive. As one of the consequences market-share dropped heavily back in 2018 as the competitor Unilever with brands like Dove outperformed them due to excellent implementations of digital marketing strategies and a strategy for communicating in the ”new” Era.

The fact that communication and marketing are key in any business development strategy is unquestionable, yet businesses can have the most amazing products or services, yet unless one is able to communicate successfully with target market, one is unlikely to see any actual results – so strategy and optimal execution of marketing is key.

In a digital age, companies are often faced with the challenge of distributing budget and efforts between engaging in digital push marketing vs. [pull-marketing](https://www.gomogroup.com/en/services/pull-marketing/) activities. However, effective marketing is only optimal when digital **pull** and **push marketing** practices are complementing strategies to achieve business objectives. Even then, most CMOs often hold back from using possible effective push marketing strategies in digital marketing strategies due to the common notion that most customers do not respond well to those types of activities, this is especially true in the FMCG segment (much like Procter & Gamble example above).

According to a study conducted by [Chron](https://smallbusiness.chron.com/examples-push-pull-marketing-20728.html) , one will be surprised to know that more conventional push-marketing methods are still very effective when it comes to building relationships. All a marketer needs to understand is how to effectively carry out digital push-marketing strategies and combine them with pull-marketing efforts effectively! In our previous articles, we have often stressed the benefits of pull marketing. However, to give our readers a more holistic view of an effective digital marketing strategy, we will discuss the importance of considering push strategies as part of an organization’s overall marketing activities. To do just that, the first step is to fully understand what exactly digital push marketing is all about.

## A Deeper Understanding of Push Marketing

While pull-marketing is all about capitalizing on existing demand, push-marketing is focused on the increase and generate demand. As such, push-marketing is also known as outbound marketing, as it pushes your communication directly to users. [Typically](https://medium.com/digital-reflections/push-vs-pull-marketing-or-both-b2c4ceb505c0) , businesses use push-marketing tactics to promote new product (s) or offer (s).

After gaining a basic understanding of digital push-marketing, let’s look at how to execute push-marketing, in the digital space, in the most effective way?

Essentially, there are multiple ways to carry out push marketing, some of which include (but not limited to):

- Display Advertising
- Online Syndication
- Online Event Promotions
- TV / Radio Advertising
- Trade Shows
- Email Marketing
- Campaign websites
- blogging
- Influencer Marketing
- Social Media Advertising (SOME Ads)
- Search Engine Advertising (SEA)
- Telemarketing (TM)

For this article, we have shortlisted two effective activities; email marketing and telemarketing. We have chosen telemarketing since its getting more and more complex and in data shows it (still) works great if made properly. Here are some statistics about email marketing and Telemarketing:

- According to [LinkedIn](https://www.slideshare.net/hschulze/marketing-automation-trends-2014), almost 90% of marketing managers claim telesales and telephone follow-up calls are an effective lead nurturing technique.
- According to [DMA](https://dma.org.uk/uploads/misc/5a7c1de1ca4d7-marketer-email-tracking-report-2018_v2-final_5a7c1de1ca425.pdf), for every $1 you spend on email marketing, you can expect an average return of $32.
- According to Emarsys, 81% of SMBs still rely on email as their primary customer acquisition channel and 80% for retention.

Like mentioned before, to execute digital push-marketing activities, it is important to carry it out effectively. If not, your business won’t receive sufficient Return on Marketing Investment (ROMI). To give you a better understanding of Email and Telemarketing, we have provided a couple of general parameters to help you understand the ‘WHEN’, ‘HOW’ and ‘WHY’ of email Marketing and telemarketing. In this process, we also got some vital insights from our in-house expert on the subject, [Anuvinder Singh](https://www.gomogroup.com/en/team/). Before joining GO MO Group, Anuvinder co-founded Inventive SMI, which focused on providing demand generation services. Within 4 years, Anuvinder grew the company from an employee strength of zero to 250 employees. Today, he leads the Online Acceleration Team at GO MO Group.

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/2-1.jpg.webp)

## The Why, When and How of Email Marketing

Email marketing, as the name suggests, allows an organization to communicate with their existing or potential customers via electronic mail. In the digital era, it’s not surprising that email marketing has become an extremely essential tool for businesses. While the benefits of email marketing cannot be denied, when is this activity most beneficial for a business?

#### The “When”

- **Cost-Effectiveness**


According to a study conducted by the [Direct Market Association](https://www.fatrabbitcreative.com/blog/5-key-benefits-of-email-marketing), if a business wants to reach a large audience cost-effectively, email marketing is the way to go! The study found that on average, email marketing brings in $40 for ever $1 spent
- **Customer Accessibility**


With the help of email marketing, businesses can reach their customers fast. In today’s digital era, people access their emails not just on a computer, but on their phones as well. Hence, organizations can get almost immediate access to their customers at all times.
- **Measurability**


With the analytics available today, it’s easy to track responses to your email campaigns exactly, to work out what parts of your campaign are working and what parts aren’t. Certain things which you should track are:


1. How many users from your email list opened the email?
2. How many users from the ones who opened the email took the desired action, for example, filling out a form
3. What was the bounce rate of the email campaign?
4. What was the success rate of different campaigns targeting the same group, but had different copy and creatives?

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/3.jpg.webp)

> “While the conversion ratio changes depending on different industries and niches, in my experience on average, the conversion ratio of email marketing is between 4% to 5%, which is much higher than other forms of marketing, like social media. The social media conversion rate is around [0.79%](https://www.adweek.com/digital/john-stevens-hostingfacts-reviews-guest-post-4-tips-for-building-a-social-media-conversion-strategy/).

_– Anuvinder Singh_

#### The “How”

According to a recent study conducted by Campaigner, 49% of consumers say they receive too many emails from businesses and marketers. Hence, if you’re looking to conduct email marketing for your business, it is essential to follow certain steps that ensure your message reaches the customer and desired goals are achieved. With the help of Anuvinder’s insights, we’ve created certain steps to follow to create the perfect email marketing strategy:

- **Don’t Mail & Miss**


For for this activity to work, it is of utmost importance that you target the right people. Or else, the email will go directly to the spam folder or ‘get trashed’ before the consumer even opens the mail. Some factors to keep in mind while creating your email list are:


1. Have the receivers ‘opted-in’ to get the email? This step is important especially in Europe to comply with GDPR
2. Are you targeting new or existing customers? This will help you determine the tone of the email and how much information you need to provide about your business
3. Are you branding the campaign from a first-party or third-party perspective? Success ratio might vary depending on campaign goals.

> “Recently, we did an email campaign for a major recycling company in Sweden, which has a turnover of almost 1 billion dollars. The target audience for the campaign was existing customers. Based on the interests of the audience, we tailor-made a campaign, for which we received high conversions, with the open rate being at 31% and the click-through rate at 12%! Understanding the audience and tailoring your strategy accordingly is the key to success for any email marketing campaign.”

_– Anuvinder Singh_

- **Get Creative**


After creating your email list, you need to design a creative that caters to your target audience. Based on their interests and preferences, understand what they would look for while purchasing a product or service. Here are some basic tips to keep in mind while creating the copy and design of your creative:


1. **Content:** The first thing to keep in mind is the subject line. Like any other piece of content, your subject line will determine if the user will even open your email or not
2. **Design:** You don’t want your email to be just text. The design of your creative is important, hence, ensure you choose an appealing color and easy-to-read fonts.

> “The creative is arguably the most important factor of your email marketing campaign. In my experience, I have seen that campaigns that have a well-made creative, on average, receive 75% higher open rates compared to campaigns with just text. ”

_– Anuvinder Singh_

- **Land a Customer**


Don’t just send your customers to your home page; instead, send them to a page where they can interact and connect with your organization. It is recommended to send the customer to one of the following pages to convert a lead:


1. Service Page
2. Product Page
3. Contact Us Page
- **Practice Makes Champions**


Your email marketing campaign is a representation of your organization. Hence, before sending it to the target audience, you need to ensure everything is perfect. You could run an internal campaign to conduct beta testing, in which you can check for the following:


1. Is the load time too long?
2. Is your creative mobile-friendly?
3. Are there any errors in the copy?
- **Success Is In The Tracking**


As mentioned earlier, a huge benefit of email marketing is the ability to easily measure the effectiveness of the campaign. Following are certain key areas that help determine how successful your campaign is:


1. Delivery Rate
2. Open Rate
3. Click-Through Rate
4. Conversion on Landing Page
5. Unsubscription Rate
6. Total ROMI of the Campaign

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/4-1.jpg.webp)

#### The “Why”

So, now that you’ve followed the steps and created and put an effective email marketing campaign into motion, what outcome should you expect?

- **Leads:**Information of potential customers for your business that is ready to be part of your sales funnel. Email marketing can help you get the following type of leads:

1. Market Qualified Leads (MQL)
2. Sales Qualified Leads (SQL)
- **Identify Outliers:** Determine which users in your email list are not interested in your organization and stop catering to those resources
- **Understanding User Behavior:** Depending on the response you receive, you get insights into what the consumer is expecting from an organization and how you can adjust your future campaigns to cater to their requirements for a better response

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/5.jpg.webp)

## Another Way of Creating Demand

Telemarketing is a push-marketing activity, where a marketer solicits prospective customers through the phone or via web conferencing. It is popularly used to promote products or services, gather information, generate leads, or carry out surveys. What makes telemarketing popular is that it saves time and money as compared to personal selling, but offers many of the same benefits related to direct contact with the customer. That being said, not every business needs telemarketing. So, when should a business conduct telemarketing?

#### When Do You Need TM?

- **Verify Data**


With the help of telemarketing, you can verify data related to potential customers quickly, while opening a two-way dialogue between you and your consumer. The data you can verify includes:


1. Identifying who are the decision maker(s)?
2. Understand if the target(s) are interested in your product
3. Validate the authenticity of prospect(s)
- **Understand Your Customer**


Telemarketing is a commonly used activity to conduct market research as it gives you consumer feedback first-hand. An organization can directly speak to the consumer, understand their issues, likes and dislikes , and develop their product and/or service according to the needs of the market.
- **Nurturing Is the Key**


After validating the data and confirming that the prospect is interested in your product or service, telemarketing can be used for the following:


1. Scheduling a web-conference call to discuss a potential sale
2. Set up a demo of your product or service
3. Schedule a face-to-face meeting to fasten the sales process

> “Telemarketing is very effective for organizations, especially when it comes to building a list of potential clients. While the data may vary depending on the industry, on average, 3% to 5% of the total number of people you call are willing to provide you with the information required or engage with your organization”.

_– Anuvinder Singh_

#### How Should You Do It?

- **Preparation Is a Must**
1. **Keep Things Civil:** Some of your customers are inevitably going to decline your offer, and that’s okay. What’s not okay, however, is to push too far or to end the call in a way, which can cause the consumer to have a negative impression of your company.
2. **Practice Makes Perfect:** You don’t want to waste the time of your customers and want to sound confident on the call. So it is recommended to conduct a couple of mock-calls before the actual call.
3. **Consider Time Zones:** Timing is immeasurably important in phone conversations. One way to fail in marketing is ‘disturbing’ people late at night or during busy office hours. Therefore, plan adequately and phone your potential clients when they are most likely free or relaxed.
- **Time For Action**


To get the best ROI for all your efforts, it is important to carefully identify who would actually be interested in your product or service. Here are some considerations you could keep in mind: Focus on the Right-Party Contact (RPC)


Ensure you have the updated information of the prospect you’re going to contact


If you’re running a campaign in Europe, ensure you have complied with the GDPR before calling a prospect


You should create a ‘Do Not Call’ (DNC) list to ensure you don’t call the same people repeatedly


Ensure you create a follow-up list, where you can recall a person if they don’t answer in the first attempt. However, always keep a set ‘waiting period’ before contacting a lead again to avoid spamming them
- **Don’t Forget to Deliver**


During the call, if you make a commitment to the customer, for example sending some marketing material, you should adhere to the commitment. According to the ‘Sun Down Rule’, you should complete all the deliverables promised to a customer by the end of that working day. This ensures that the customer feels valued and is not left waiting for the information required.

> “Traditionally, most marketers perceive telemarketing as a “forceful” activity that causes more harm than good. However, similar to a “weapon”, if not used correctly, you can end-up hurt yourself. On the other hand, if used well, telemarketing can give your sales funnel a major boost. 78% of decision-makers have accepted appointments or attended events that can from a sales call. For example, you can create an email marketing campaign, which caters to a very niche target audience, and within that campaign, the client can opt for a call-back to get a product demo from your team. These types of customized strategies, in most cases, leads to positive results.”

_– Anuvinder Singh_

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/6-1.jpg.webp)

#### Why Should You Do It?

So, now that you’ve followed the steps and executed the perfect telemarketing campaign, what outcome should you expect?

- **Market Intelligence:** If you conduct a survey, the information provided to you in real-time gives you a great understanding of what the consumer is looking, if you can meet their requirements and if the contact information you have is of the decision-makers of the company.
- **Nurture Leads:** Businesses can make use of this activity to move the prospect to the next level in the sales process, which is given below:

1. Contact leads to get confirmation clear interest in the product or service
2. Establish timeline: in detail understand when the client can make a purchase
3. Schedule a web demonstration of your product or service
4. Schedule a face-to-face appointment with the customer

## Conclusion

We have compiled this analysis after conducting thorough research, experiments, and analyzes of real-life case studies. It is important to understand that the outcome of email marketing and telemarketing is heavily dependent on the industry, product, and target audience. Hence, it is essential to stay up-to-date on the latest trends and techniques to effectively implement email marketing and telemarketing. We welcome feedback and suggestions regarding our blogs, so please feel free to write to us! Till then, keep reading our blogs for tips and tricks, and make the best use of digital marketing for your business.

Generative AI, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) \| READING TIME: 6 MINUTES \| October 15, 2026

# Do visitors from ChatGPT and other AI assistants convert better?

**GO MO research · AI search · July–September 2026**

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ai-visitors-convert-better-image.webp)

Yes. Across 60+ websites, AI visitors converted at nearly twice the rate of other visitors to the same site. Industry decides the size of the gain, and for software companies the result reverses.

**GO MO Group** · 250+ Google Analytics 4 properties reviewed · 90 days of data

The short answer

## How much better do AI visitors convert?

Nearly twice as well. AI visitors converted at about 2x the rate of the other visitors on the same website, and they did so on 8 in 10 sites.

They stayed about as long, close to a minute per session. Two in three AI visits were engaged, against three in five for other traffic.

AI assistants still send a small share of traffic: about 1% of all sessions. ChatGPT sent over 90% of those visits.

~2xConversion rateAI visitors compared with the same site's other visitors.

8 in 10Sites where AI converted betterThe typical result held on most sites.

~1%Share of all sessionsOver 90% of AI visits came from ChatGPT.

_30 June to 27 September 2026. All figures are rounded._

**250+** GA4 properties reviewed **60+** websites with enough AI traffic to compare **Nordic** B2B, education and e-commerce companies

The questions this article answers

- “Does traffic from ChatGPT convert better than traffic from Google?”
- “Is AI search traffic worth optimising for in B2B?”
- “Why does AI traffic in my GA4 look worse than other channels?”

These are the questions marketing teams ask us, and the way they ask them in ChatGPT and Google. Each section below opens with its answer.

**What is an AI visit?** A session that arrived from an AI assistant such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity or Claude.

**What is a conversion?** A session in which the visitor completed one of the site's key events, such as a form, a purchase or a booking.

**What is the baseline?** The same site's other visitors in the same 90 days. Every site is compared with itself.

Four actions

## What should marketing teams do with their AI traffic?

Check that it is real, compare it with your own site, and build the landing page for the stage the visitor is at.

01

**Is your AI traffic real?** Break AI sessions down by country, device and landing page before you report them. On one site in our study, 9 in 10 “ChatGPT” visits were automated.

02

**What is your own baseline?** Compare AI visitors with your site’s other visitors. Each site defines a conversion its own way, so benchmarks from other sites will mislead you.

03

**What stage is the visitor at?** E-commerce visitors from AI arrive ready to buy, so shorten the path to checkout. Software visitors arrive to research, so lead with comparison and pricing content.

04

**Are you counting every assistant?** GA4’s AI assistant channel catches ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. Add your own channel rule so Perplexity and Claude visits are counted as AI too.

Hypothesis

## Why is our result lower than the 23x in the headlines?

Because the biggest numbers come from single websites. Across 60+ sites, the typical uplift is about 2x.

We expected to confirm the uplift everyone quotes. Ahrefs reported that AI visitors converted about 23 times better on its own site. Conductor's benchmark put the figure at about 4x.

A study of 973 e-commerce sites by the University of Hamburg pointed the other way: ChatGPT visitors converted slightly below organic search visitors.

Our result sits between the two. We believe the method explains most of the gap. A single site with a strong product can show a large uplift. Comparing each of 60+ sites with itself gives the typical result.

> Plan on AI visitors converting at about twice your site's normal rate. Then test that figure on your own data.

Reported uplift for AI visitors, by study

StudyUplift

Ahrefs, 1 site~23x

Conductor~4x

**GO MO, 60+ sites** ~2x

Hamburg, 973 sitesjust under 1x

_Bars drawn to a linear scale. The studies use different comparison traffic: organic search (Ahrefs, Hamburg), all other traffic (Conductor) and the same site's other visitors (GO MO)._

Industry groups

## Which industries gain the most from AI visitors?

E-commerce gains the most, education and industry follow closely, and software and finance lose. The results fall into three groups, set by how far along the buying process the visitor is when they arrive.

AI visitors' conversion rate compared with the same site's other visitors

IndustryResult

E-commerceover 2x

Educationabout 2x

Manufacturing and industryover 1.5x

Software and finance20% below

_The typical (median) site in each industry. Manufacturing and industry includes construction and recycling. The e-commerce and the software and finance groups each have fewer than 10 sites._

GROUP 1 · E-COMMERCE

### **Decided buyers: they browse less and buy more**

AI visitors spent about a third less time on e-commerce sites, and still converted at over twice the normal rate. The pattern held on every e-commerce site with purchase tracking.

**Our hypothesis:** the assistant has already compared the products. The visitor clicks through to buy the one it recommended.

**What to do:** make the product page an AI visitor lands on the shortest route to checkout.

GROUP 2 · EDUCATION AND INDUSTRY

### **Shortlisters: they stay longer and ask for more**

In education, AI visitors converted at about twice the normal rate, on 9 in 10 sites. In manufacturing and industry the gain was over 1.5x, also on 9 in 10 sites. These are the two largest groups in the study, so the result is the most reliable.

**Our hypothesis:** the visitor asked the assistant for a shortlist of schools or suppliers. They arrive to confirm a choice, so they request information, apply or ask for a quote.

**What to do:** put the facts people check on a shortlist (entry requirements, specifications, lead times, prices) on the first page they see.

GROUP 3 · SOFTWARE AND FINANCE

### **Researchers: they compare and leave**

This is the one group where AI visitors converted below the baseline, about 20% lower. Time on site was similar to other visitors.

**Our hypothesis:** people ask assistants to compare software tools and funds early in the process. They click through to check one detail. The conversion on these sites is usually a demo request or an account opening, which is a big step for someone still comparing.

**What to do:** give AI visitors comparison and pricing pages, and a smaller next step than a demo: a price calculator, a checklist or a short product video.

> One caution: the software and finance group has fewer than 10 sites. Treat it as a strong signal to test on your own site, and give the education and industry results the most weight.

The outliers

## Why does AI traffic look bad in some GA4 reports?

In our data, the main reason was automated traffic. On one e-commerce site, about 9 in 10 visits labelled as ChatGPT came from a bot.

That single site made up 60% of all AI sessions in the study. With it included, AI visitors looked shorter-staying and lower-converting than the average visitor. Once we removed it, the overall result reversed.

**Our hypothesis:** an automated tool, such as a scraper or a price monitor, sent the ChatGPT referrer with its requests. The visits came in one large burst, from one country outside the site's markets, and almost none engaged.

Three other sites had broken tracking: two recorded a conversion on every session, and one had a baseline full of bot visits. We removed all four sites before comparing.

Sign of automated trafficAre most AI sessions on desktop from one country?Compare the country split of AI visits with your other traffic. A country outside your markets, holding most AI sessions, needs a closer look.

Sign of automated trafficDid the sessions arrive in one short burst?Plot AI sessions by day. Human AI traffic grows steadily. A single month with ten times the usual volume points to a tool.

Sign of automated trafficIs the landing page "(not set)"?Real visitors land on a page. Large numbers of sessions with no landing page usually come from automated requests.

Sign of broken trackingIs every session a conversion?A conversion rate close to 100% on any channel means the key event fires on page load. Fix the event before comparing channels.

> If AI traffic looks like your worst channel, check whether it is real before you change any pages.

By assistant

## Does it matter which AI assistant sent the visitor?

Only in volume. ChatGPT sent over 90% of AI visits. Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity and Claude sent the rest.

Visitors from every assistant stayed about a minute per session. ChatGPT visitors converted slightly more often, but the other assistants sent too few visits for a reliable comparison.

For now, optimise for the questions people ask ChatGPT, and track every assistant so you see when the mix changes.

ChatGPTGeminiCopilotPerplexityClaude

Check your own data

## How do you measure AI visitors in GA4?

Five steps, in this order. The whole check takes about an hour for one property.

01

Count every AI assistantIn GA4, create a custom channel group with an "AI assistants" channel above Referral. Use a session source rule that matches this pattern:`chatgpt|openai|perplexity|claude\.ai|gemini\.google|copilot|deepseek|grok|mistral|kagi`Leave out paid ChatGPT ad clicks, which arrive with sources such as "chatgpt\_ad". Count them as paid media.

02

Remove automated and broken sessionsCheck AI sessions by country, device, day and landing page, using the signs in the section above. Exclude what fails the check and write down what you removed.

03

Compare AI with your own baselineCompare the AI channel's key-event rate, engagement rate and engagement time with all other sessions on the same property, over the same dates.

04

Split by page type and marketLook at which pages AI visitors land on and which markets they come from. This shows where the gain comes from, and which pages to improve first.

05

Match the page to the visitor's stageDecided buyers need a short path to purchase. Shortlisters need the facts they check. Researchers need comparisons and a small next step.

Methodology

## How did we measure the difference?

**What data did we use?** First-party Google Analytics 4 data from every property GO MO manages, 250+ in total, pulled through the GA4 Data API. 60+ websites had enough AI traffic to compare.

**Which period did we cover?** 90 days, from 30 June to 27 September 2026.

**How did we compare sites?** For each site, we compared AI visitors with the same site's other visitors. We then took the typical (median) site. This method holds up because each site defines its own key events.

**How were industries grouped?** Using SNI 2025, Sweden's industry classification, merged into broader themes. Client names are withheld. Health and care and business services had too few sites to report separately.

**What did we exclude?** Sites with fewer than 100 AI sessions, one site with automated ChatGPT-referred traffic, and three sites with broken tracking.

**What are the limits?** This is GO MO's client sample of Nordic companies, weighted towards education and industry. AI visits with no referrer appear as Direct in GA4, so the true AI share is likely higher than 1%.

_A conversion is a session with at least one GA4 key event. Ratios compare the AI conversion rate with the baseline conversion rate on the same site. All figures are rounded._

Related questions

## What else should marketing teams know?

Does ChatGPT traffic convert better than Google traffic?

In our data, yes. AI visitors, over 90% of them from ChatGPT, converted at about twice the rate of the same site's other visitors, Google included. The gain is largest in e-commerce and smallest in software.

Is AI search traffic worth optimising for if it is only 1% of visits?

Yes, if those visits convert at twice the normal rate. In that case 1% of sessions brings about 2% of conversions. Start with the pages AI visitors already land on.

Why do AI visitors spend less time on e-commerce sites?

They arrive having already compared products in the assistant. They go straight to the product and buy it, which shortens the visit and raises the conversion rate.

Where does GA4 put ChatGPT traffic?

Since May 2026, GA4 files recognised AI referrals under the AI assistant channel, with the medium "ai-assistant". Some Perplexity and Claude visits still land in Referral, and visits with no referrer land in Direct. A custom channel rule catches more of them.

How can you tell real AI visits from bots?

Real AI visitors land on a page, come from your markets, use a mix of devices and grow steadily over time. Automated traffic arrives in bursts, from one country and one device, with no landing page.

What should software companies change for AI visitors?

Change what AI visitors find when they arrive. In our data, software visitors from AI came to research. Give them comparison pages, clear pricing and a smaller first step, such as a price calculator, alongside the demo form.

**Research source:** GO MO analysis of anonymised, first-party Google Analytics 4 data, 30 June to 27 September 2026.

**Other studies cited:** [Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/blog/chat-gpt-traffic), [Conductor benchmark (via Lantern)](https://www.asklantern.com/blogs/chatgpt-drives-87-of-ai-referral-traffic), [University of Hamburg study of 973 e-commerce sites](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/rosspjohnson_this-well-designed-study-found-that-chatgpt-activity-7391499381461405696-lIvW), [Clique Studios on the GA4 AI assistant channel](https://cliquestudios.com/university/resources/ga4-ai-assistant-channel). # AI-Generated Content: A Strategic Advantage for B2B CMOs

> Revolutionize B2B Marketing with AI-Generated Content and Human Expertise

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/AI-text-article-in-text-image.jpeg.webp)

In today’s competitive B2B landscape, CMOs are constantly seeking innovative strategies to elevate their brand’s visibility and drive growth. One ground-breaking innovation is the use of AI-generated content, a subject that has piqued the interest of many clients. By leveraging AI-generated content responsibly, B2B CMOs can transform their marketing strategies and stay ahead of the competition by increasing content output by some 50-100 %.

## I. The Power of AI-generated Content:

Ignite a B2B marketing revolution by wielding AI-generated content as your ultimate weapon. Skillfully merge it with human expertise to amplify the [E-E-A-T framework](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2022/12/google-raters-guidelines-e-e-a-t), deliver exceptional user experiences, captivate your audience, and outperform the competition in the dynamic digital marketing arena.

## II. Google’s Caution on AI-generated Content:

[Google cautions against using automatically generated content](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/02/google-search-and-ai-content) for manipulative purposes in search rankings. However, when employed responsibly, AI-generated content can be a transformative asset for B2B marketing strategies.

> “Our focus on the quality of content, rather than how content is produced, is a useful guide that has helped us deliver reliable, high quality results to users for years.” _– Google Search Central_

## III. Enhancing the E-E-A-T Framework with AI-generated Content:

The E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authority, and Trustworthiness) framework is undeniably crucial. Incorporating AI-generated content can enhance these factors when skillfully combined with human expertise. The key is to utilize AI as a powerful ally, ensuring the content produced is not only of high quality but also delivers value to your target audience.

## IV. Key Considerations for B2B CMOs:

As a B2B CMO, consider these thought-provoking questions when evaluating your AI-generated content strategy:

1. Are you capitalizing on AI’s unique capabilities to amplify the experience, expertise, authority, and trustworthiness of your content?
2. How are you integrating human editing and curation to refine the AI-generated output and ensure it meets your audience’s expectations?
3. Is the information provided accurate, up-to-date, and comprehensive, reflecting the latest industry insights and trends?
4. Does the AI-generated content align with your brand’s voice, personality, and experience, ensuring a seamless integration?

### Conclusion:

Embrace AI-generated content to transform your B2B marketing strategy, elevating the E-E-A-T framework and delivering exceptional user experiences. Stay ahead of the competition in the ever-evolving digital landscape by combining AI innovation with human expertise. Adopt this powerful duo to revolutionize your marketing approach and secure a strategic advantage in the B2B market.

# AI Forces Realignment in Marketing: GO MO Group’s strategic shift towards self-governing niche agencies

**GOTHENBURG, Sweden; June 7th, 2023 –** In our view, the future belongs to those who shape it. With this belief in mind, B2B marketing agency GO MO Group is taking proactive steps to shape an [AI-driven future](https://www.gomogroup.com/insikter/gabriel-ghavami/framtidens-marknadsforing-chatgpt3/). The company is transitioning from a generalist marketing agency into a collective of autonomous “niche marketing agencies.” We believe that each of these specialized entities, dedicated to serving one of the three key B2B market sectors (global giants, SaaS scale-ups, small- & medium-sized enterprises), will position us not just as relevant but as leaders in the ever-evolving marketing landscape.

According to GO MO Group’s founder and CEO, [Gabriel Ghavami](https://www.gomogroup.com/medarbetare/gabriel-ghavami/): “By harnessing the power of AI in combination with human expertise and creating these specialized niche agencies, we are paving the way for our continued success.”

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%202240%201260'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Ghavami recognizes the need for earlier action, stating, “In our view, the AI revolution has made change an imperative, not a choice. We aim to inspire others to embrace paradigm shifts as catalysts for transformation.” As per our understanding, AI does not replace the human element; instead, it enhances our capabilities. The synergy between humans and machines empowers us to adapt and thrive in the evolving marketing landscape.

Our primary objective is to establish an agile and responsive structure that allows each segment to benefit from specialized and cross-functional teams, who possess a deep understanding of their specific market dynamics. We believe that fostering strong ownership and enhancing decision-making processes aligned with the needs of each segment will be key to our success. We are departing from the ‘one size fits all’ approach, as per our understanding that it is no longer viable in today’s dynamic and diverse business ecosystem.

At the core of our innovative approach is the collaboration between GO MO Group’s offices in Sweden and India. We firmly believe that this fusion of global talent and cutting-edge technology creates a powerful blend of human creativity and AI efficiency.

![Gabriel Ghavami om tankeledarskap inom B2B marknadsföring](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%202260%201260'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

As part of our shift, we have set ambitious goals to grow these niche agencies tenfold within five years. We are committed to employee satisfaction and continuous skill development in areas such as [SEO](https://www.gomogroup.com/en/services/seo-search-engine-optimization/), paid digital advertising, digital design, web development, and [AI-driven content creation](https://www.gomogroup.com/insights/embracing-ai-generated-content-a-strategic-advantage/).

In this pivotal period marked by tech-driven transformation, shifting B2B buying behaviors, and economic recession, we are boldly reshaping the B2B marketing landscape and leading the way forward with unwavering determination and innovative spirit.

_For more information, please contact Timothy Larsson at [timothy@gomogroup.com](mailto:timothy@gomogroup.com) or the co-author Chat-GPT 4.0._

# Engineering Students Build Their Way Into Digital Marketing

If engineering was a religion, it will count as the fifth most populous in India! In fact, a record-breaking 1.4 million candidates appeared for the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE), or more commonly known as the entrance exam for engineers in 2018. However, recently a large number of engineering graduates are either unemployed or work as blue-collared labourers, especially computer engineers who traditionally banked on the IT sector to provide them with job opportunities. With the stagnation of growth in the IT sector, more than [80%](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/jobs/employability-survey-2019-jobs-slip-away-from-the-ill-equipped-indian-engineer/articleshow/68559686.cms?from=mdr) of Indian computer engineers are unemployed and around 222,000 computer engineering graduates applied for peon posts.

That being said, with the rise of the [digital marketing](https://www.gomogroup.com/) industry, a new opportunity has emerged for engineers. Consequently, plenty of engineers are finding work in the digital marketing industry.

So, what makes the digital marketing world enticing for engineers? It’s simple. What are the most common traits of an engineer?

- They are creators
- They like research
- They like creating strategies
- They believe in experimentation

Coincidentally, (or not!) these are some of the most common traits required to be a successful digital marketer as well. Hence, it’s evident that the skills of an engineer are more than welcome in the digital marketing industry.

> _“As an engineering graduate, I chose to pursue a career in digital marketing due to numerous reasons. The major one is job sustainability. With the IT sector facing the consequences of the recession, while the digital marketing industry still continues to grow, it was a no-brainer making this career shift. Plus, thanks to the numerous channels in the field of digital marketing, the growth opportunities are limitless!”_

_– Tejas Salvi, Management Associate at GO MO Group_

## GO MO Takes The Stage

The opening of a new career opportunity for engineers has not gone unnoticed by prestigious colleges and institutes. With an aim to provide only the best to their students, these institutes started inviting digital marketing companies for campus placements. One such institution was the Symbiosis Institute of Technology (SIT). However, the institutes noticed that while students were intrigued by digital marketing, they weren’t fully aware of the scope of opportunities present for them.

Owing to this, the college invited us to spread awareness about the digital marketing niche as industry experts. Hence, [Akshat Bharani](https://www.linkedin.com/in/akshat-bharani/), the Team Lead of SEO and [Kunal Baja](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kunal-bajaj-9916b418/) [j](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kunal-bajaj-9916b418/), Partner and Senior Project Manager at GO MO Group visited [Symbiosis Institute of Technology](https://www.sitpune.edu.in/). With over 100 students in attendance, the objective of this visit was to spread awareness among their students about the rise of digital marketing and how it can be a viable career option for engineering students.

![Kunal presenterar karriärmöjligheter inom digital marknadsföring | GO MO Group](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20900%20600'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

> _“The aim of these workshops is not to convince anyone, rather we are here to present an alternative opportunity that these students were not aware of. This helps them make an informed decision with respect to their career.”_

_– Kunal Bajaj, Partner & Sr. Project Manager at GO MO Group._

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20600%20600'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## A Rendezvous With Kunal Bajaj

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20900%20601'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

After the presentation, we had a quick chat with Kunal to get insights on his experiences and get a better understanding of the current scenario in the digital marketing niche. With the introduction of giants like Zomato and Uber who are disrupting the entire job market, Kunal believes that engineers are attracted to the digital marketing niche due to the vast range of job opportunities available. He went on to state that in his experience a lot of the engineering students actually have a passion for management, marketing and business. Digital marketing allows these students to explore subjects that they are interested in, but don’t get the opportunity in engineering jobs.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20900%20600'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

When questioned about the skills engineers had to help them fit in the digital marketing universe, Kunal stated, “They are engineers! I mean, besides having the technical, analytical and logical skills, they are true hard-workers. These students have come from an environment where they have to cram the knowledge of 20 subjects in one night while juggling assignments and workshops. They know how to deal with pressure and multi-task effectively. That’s exactly what we want in a digital marketer!”

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20900%20601'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

On a final note, when asked to give some advice to young minds that are considering to opt for the digital marketing industry, Kunal said, “Don’t choose a field just for the sake of choosing. Or, don’t choose a field under peer or parental pressure. Choose a field that you are really passionate about. If your passion lies in digital marketing, then roll up your sleeves and get to learning. You cannot succeed in this field with half knowledge and to be an expert you need to keep learning and upgrading your knowledge. Being a digital marketer requires a lot of hard work and “average” just doesn’t work. Hence, you need to be willing to invest your all, and when you do, the benefits are truly worth the effort”.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20900%20601'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

> _I believe engineers make good digital marketers because they are tech-savvy, and digital marketing is all about technology. Moreover, engineers are hardworking and deadline-oriented due to the most complex evaluation happening in engineering right and now and the introduction of new opportunities come at an opportune moment! I appreciate Mr Kunal Bajaj, Akshat Bharani and Ankita Samant for all their efforts to make this presentation happen._

_– Dr Nilisha, Placement Coordinator, SIT_

# From AI hype to real implementation inside modern organisations

In this conversation, [**Henrik Andereberg**](https://www.gomogroup.com/en/team/henrik-anderberg/), digital strategist at [**GO MO Group**](https://www.gomogroup.com/en/), explores how generative AI has evolved from early hype to a powerful technological shift already reshaping knowledge work. Reflecting on the rapid rise of tools like ChatGPT, he discusses why AI adoption inside companies still lags behind technological progress, the growing divide between early adopters and organisations, and what leaders must do to move from experimentation to real implementation across teams and workflows.

Since the emergence of tools like ChatGPT in 2022, generative AI has advanced rapidly. What began as experimentation is now entering daily workflows, though organizational adoption is still early.

Generative AI is more than a productivity tool. It is reshaping knowledge work, with intelligent systems supporting analysis, generating insights, and assisting decisions while workers increasingly guide and oversee these systems.

> “Technologically the progress has been incredibly fast. But adoption within companies is still surprisingly slow.”

## The great divide in AI adoption

Despite rapid technological progress, **AI adoption across organizations remains uneven**. Some individuals already use AI tools daily, integrating them into their workflows and decision making. **Many companies, however, are still in early experimentation stages**. This creates a **growing divide between those actively leveraging AI and those still observing from the sidelines**, where the technology exists and works, but its benefits are not yet widely realised.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20960%20540'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## Three stages of AI adoption

Organisations are currently adopting generative AI at very different speeds. While some companies remain in early experimentation, others are beginning to scale usage across teams and workflows. Broadly, AI adoption tends to evolve through three stages, moving from isolated experimentation to structured rollout and eventually to deep integration into everyday operations.

1\. What does early stage AI experimentation begin in companies?

AI adoption often starts organically. Individuals experiment with tools independently without a company wide strategy. While this helps teams discover possibilities, the overall impact remains limited without leadership direction.

2\. How do companies go from experimentation to structured AI adoption?

Organisations begin introducing training, leadership support, and clear expectations for daily AI use. This helps move from isolated experimentation to broader adoption across teams and workflows.

3\. What happens when AI becomes fully integrated in business?

AI becomes embedded across workflows, systems, and decision making. Organizations redesign how work is performed, turning AI from a tool into a core part of operations.

## Why companies struggle with adoption

One of the biggest **barriers to AI adoption is not the technology itself but organisational leadership**. Many companies experiment with small pilot initiatives without establishing a clear direction for broader transformation. Without strategic leadership and structured implementation, the impact of AI often remains limited.

> “One of the biggest challenges is what I call ‘incremental leadership’. Instead of making AI a central priority, companies give a few people licenses here and there. That does not change the organization.”

## The GO MO approach to leadership in the age of AI

Generative AI technology has advanced rapidly, but the **real challenge now lies in organisational adoption**. Many companies are still experimenting with isolated tools, yet meaningful transformation requires leadership that sets clear priorities and guides teams from experimentation to everyday use.

From a [**GO MO Group**](https://www.gomogroup.com/en/) perspective, successful organisations approach AI **adoption as a structured capability building journey**. When leadership commitment is combined with training, experimentation, and practical use cases, AI moves beyond hype and becomes a driver of productivity, innovation, and long term competitive advantage.

# From Uddevalla to Global Markets

_The case was first published in 2024 — and has since been continuously updated, with the work still ongoing as of March 2026. The journey has evolved and deepened over time. Below, we share insights from the starting point to where things stand today — and what has actually happened along the way._

**How FKAB Marine Design Began Its AI-Driven Growth Journey**

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/fkab-ship-image1-495x400-1.webp)

How can a ship design company from Uddevalla, Sweden expand globally while making its sales and marketing efforts more efficient?

For FKAB Marine Design, the answer was a combination of **strategy, data, and AI**. Together with GO MO Group, the company began an AI-driven transformation aimed at building a more targeted marketing strategy and strengthening its international presence.

## About the Company

FKAB Marine Design is a Swedish engineering and design company specializing in ship design for international markets. With deep roots in western Sweden and clients around the world, the company has long delivered innovative vessel design solutions to the maritime industry.

As the market evolves and competition increases, FKAB recognized the need to modernize its sales and marketing processes to support continued growth.

> “We want to grow and go even further, and to do that we need to keep up.”
>
> – Peter Hermansson, CEO, FKAB Marine Design

## The Challenge

FKAB faced a critical question: how can the company continue expanding globally while making its marketing efforts more efficient and data-driven?

To achieve this, the organization needed to:

- identify new international markets
- work more systematically with data and insights
- streamline marketing and sales processes
- leverage emerging technologies to stay competitive

Addressing these challenges required both **strategic analysis and new ways of working.**

## The Solution: A Strategic AI Feasibility Study

The collaboration with GO MO Group began with a comprehensive feasibility study focusing on FKAB’s market opportunities and digital demand.

The goal was to establish a clear foundation for how FKAB could integrate AI and data into its growth strategy.

The work focused on three key areas:

**Market Analysis** Identifying priority markets and assessing global demand.

**Data-Driven Marketing Strategy** Developing targeted marketing activities based on insights and analysis.

**AI-Powered Optimization** Using generative AI to support content creation, campaign optimization, and analytical processes.

The result was a clear roadmap for how FKAB can strengthen its marketing capabilities through data and AI.

## DigiShift – The Starting Point for FKAB’s AI Journey

FKAB took its first concrete steps into AI through the **DigiShift program by the West Sweden Chamber of Commerce**, where GO MO Group participates as a partner.

The program provides companies with:

- inspiration and education around AI
- access to experts
- a network of companies undergoing similar transformations

The initiative began in the summer of 2024 with the goal of building a strong foundation for targeted campaigns in selected international markets.

Throughout the process, GO MO Group acted as a strategic partner, helping FKAB translate insights into practical actions.

## Results

The collaboration has already led to several tangible improvements within the organization.

**More Precise Marketing Activities** Data-driven insights now allow FKAB to target its marketing efforts toward the most relevant markets.

**More Efficient Internal Processes** AI has helped automate parts of reporting and analytical work.

**Greater Focus on Strategic Initiatives** The management team can now spend more time on long-term decision-making and business development.

> “By automating parts of our reporting and analytical processes, we’ve been able to free up time for strategic initiatives and long-term decisions.”
>
> – Peter Hermansson

## A Shift in How Businesses Operate

For FKAB, adopting AI is not just about implementing new technology. It represents a shift in how the organization approaches decision-making, analysis, and market strategy.

> “GenAI is no longer just a buzzword. It’s a tool that is already reshaping businesses and creating new opportunities.”
>
> – Gabriel Ghavami, CEO, GO MO Group

Companies that integrate data and AI into their decision-making processes are able to move faster, work more efficiently, and identify new opportunities earlier.

## Key Takeaways from the Project

The collaboration with FKAB highlights three important insights:

**AI delivers the greatest value when tied to business goals** Technology alone does not create value without a clear strategic context.

**Data-driven decision-making creates competitive advantage** Organizations that systematically use data move faster and make better decisions.

**AI requires new ways of working** Successful implementation involves both new tools and new mindsets.

## Start Your AI Journey

Companies that invest in AI and data-driven decision-making are already gaining a significant competitive advantage.

If you’re interested in exploring how AI could strengthen your organization, or if you would like to learn more about the DigiShift program by the West Sweden Chamber of Commerce, we would be happy to talk.

At GO MO Group, we’d gladly invite you for a conversation over coffee to discuss the possibilities.

**Get in touch with us to learn how your organization can take the next step.**

Generative AI, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) \| READING TIME: 5 MINUTES \| February 20, 2025

# The Future of Search Is Here—And It’s Reshaping Digital Strategy for B2B Enterprises

## AI Has Fundamentally Reshaped SEO—And Every Digital Leader Must Adapt Now

The foundation of search is no longer what it used to be. At GO MO Group, we’ve spent the last 20 months conducting extensive research and hypothesis-driven testing to understand how AI is redefining visibility, engagement, and competition in digital search—and the conclusions are clear.

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/u5635784886_A_futuristic_digital_landscape_where_AI-driven_se_d7ce032c-5543-4c81-baba-f30291f9e370_2-1.png)

Search has fundamentally changed. AI-driven search results—Google’s AI Overviews, OpenAI’s SearchGPT, and AI-powered voice search—are no longer experimental features; they are the new default. Some facts:

- Over **64%** of Google searches now include AI-generated responses.
- Organic traffic could decline by **50%** by 2028 as AI delivers instant answers without requiring users to click.
- Traditional SEO strategies are rapidly losing impact as AI search curates content dynamically which is trained on old information (pre-training data set).

For digital experience leaders, online managers, digital marketing managers, and CMOs in global B2B enterprises, this shift isn’t just about search—it’s about how customers discover, evaluate, and interact with your brand.

The question is no longer if AI will change your search strategy. It already has. The real question is:

**Will your enterprise adapt in time—or be left behind?**

### Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): Competing Before the Click

Imagine this scenario:

A global procurement leader at a Fortune 500 company searches for: “Best sustainable manufacturing suppliers in Europe.”

Instead of the traditional list of links, AI search tools create an instant, curated response—aggregated from Google Business Profile reviews, LinkedIn endorsements, verified industry reports, and case studies.

This AI-generated summary presents a single, trusted answer—bypassing traditional SEO rankings entirely.

This is [Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)](https://www.gomogroup.com/en/services/generative-engine-optimization-geo/) in action.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20760%20426'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

GEO is the new battleground for global B2B enterprises. Instead of ranking links, AI now ranks answers. The goal is no longer just driving clicks—it’s ensuring your brand is included in AI-generated search responses.

The implications are significant:

- Google’s Gemini AI is already transforming local and enterprise-level search visibility.
- OpenAI’s SearchGPT isn’t just retrieving information—it’s contextualizing it.
- AI-powered voice search and multimodal search are changing how B2B buyers discover suppliers and solutions.

Traditional SEO tactics—keyword optimization and link-building—are no longer enough. The focus must shift toward trust, authority, and AI-driven discoverability.

### Rethinking Search Visibility in an AI-Driven World

For years, the ultimate goal was ranking on Page 1 of Google. Today, that’s no longer enough.

- **99.9%** of AI Overview results include SERP features like Featured Snippets and “People Also Ask”, altering how content is surfaced.
- **81%** of AI Overview traffic now comes from mobile devices, where instant, AI-driven answers dominate search interactions.

For digital leaders in global enterprises, this means one thing: If your content isn’t structured, optimized, and trusted by AI, it will disappear from the search landscape.

### What GEO Means for Global B2B Enterprises—Right Now

For B2B brands operating at scale, the shift to AI-driven search requires a **fundamental change in content strategy and digital visibility**.

Here’s what enterprise-level digital marketing and experience leaders need to focus on now:

**1) Own Your FAQs and Structured Content**

AI search thrives on **structured, authoritative content**. If AI can’t easily extract key insights from your website, it will **bypass your content entirely**.

- Develop in-depth FAQ sections addressing customer pain points and industry challenges.
- Implement structured data and schema markup to ensure AI understands and retrieves your content.
- Prioritize concise, authoritative, AI-friendly content that aligns with B2B buyer queries.

**2) Build an AI-Optimized Digital Reputation**

AI-driven search **does not prioritize ads or self-promotional content**—it ranks **verified insights, reviews, and credibility signals**.

- Google Business Profile (GBP) reviews and LinkedIn endorsements will shape your brand’s AI visibility.
- AI trusts peer-reviewed sources, case studies, and expert-authored content—not just keyword-optimized pages.
- Enterprise brands with strong external credibility will dominate AI-curated search results.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20737%20306'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**3) Be Everywhere AI Is Searching**

B2B search isn’t limited to Google anymore. AI search is multimodal—pulling from **text, video, voice search, and industry-specific data sources.**

- Ensure brand visibility in Google AI Overviews, OpenAI’s SearchGPT, and LinkedIn AI-generated search.
- Optimize for AI-driven voice search, where conversational queries dictate brand discovery.
- Develop high-quality, trusted B2B content that AI models can surface across multiple platforms.

### This Shift Demands a Strategic Response

The transition from SEO to GEO is more than just another evolution in digital marketing—it represents a fundamental change in how businesses are discovered and engaged with online.

For global B2B enterprises, this shift isn’t about quick fixes or chasing trends. It’s about understanding how AI-driven search is altering the buyer journey, digital visibility, and competitive positioning at a structural level.

At GO MO Group, we have dedicated the past 20 months to researching, testing, and mapping out the real-world implications of these changes. We’ve worked closely with B2B companies to understand what this means—not just in theory, but in practice.

What’s clear is that AI-powered search isn’t something businesses can afford to ignore anymore. The traditional strategies that worked before won’t be enough in a landscape where AI determines what information is trusted and shown to users.

Navigating this shift requires a long-term approach, built on expertise, adaptability, and shared insights across industries. By working together to understand and respond to these developments, digital leaders can ensure their companies remain visible, relevant, and positioned for the future.

Is your business ready for the AI-driven future of search? [Let’s talk](https://www.gomogroup.com/en/contact-us/) about how you can stay ahead.

1\. What is Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and why is it critical for B2B enterprises?

Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is a new approach to digital visibility, focusing on getting brands featured in AI-generated search responses rather than traditional blue links on Google that you have to click on. For B2B enterprises, it ensures your content is included in tools like Google’s AI Overviews and OpenAI’s ChatGPT—where modern decision-makers are searching more and more.

2\. How is the future of SEO changing with AI-powered search tools like Gemini and SearchGPT?

AI-powered tools now summarize search results instead of linking out. Platforms like Gemini and ChatGPT prioritize structured, trusted content. B2B enterprises must shift from basic keyword SEO to authoritative, AI-readable content formats to stay visible. Biggest change is that expected traffic is reducing drastically.

3\. What should B2B companies do to maintain search visibility in an AI-driven landscape?

Enterprises need to focus on structured content, digital trust signals (like reviews and third-party citations), and presence across multimodal search formats—including voice, video, and AI chat results. GEO is the strategy that supports this transformation.

# Generative AI: The Difference Between Traditional AI and a Revolutionary Force in Sales and Marketing

**Preparing your workforce in sales, marketing, and project management for the era of generative AI by building a winning corporate memory and elevating baseline capabilities. Empowering you to reinvent traditional processes in smarter, more innovative ways, ensuring you always stay ahead of the curve.**

![](https://www.gomogroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/dall-e-image.webp)

AI, or artificial intelligence, encompasses techniques that enable machines to perform tasks requiring human intelligence, such as understanding speech and identifying objects. Generative AI is an advanced form of AI that not only analyzes data but also creates new content and predicts outcomes based on large amounts of data.

In sales and marketing, generative AI enables the development of new strategies, personalized content creation, and optimized customer experiences with unprecedented speed and accuracy. By leveraging generative AI, companies can identify and exploit new growth opportunities and improve their business processes.

Generative AI differs from traditional AI through its ability to be creative and proactive, opening up innovative solutions and improved efficiency. Our insights into digital marketing are derived from hundreds of ongoing client engagements. Read about trends in digital marketing, generative AI, and the conclusions we've drawn from previous projects.

## **The Challenge of Talent and Organizational Adaptation**

Despite the promises of generative AI, there are challenges in organizational readiness and talent. Many companies have yet to fully exploit the capabilities of generative AI, primarily due to a lack of skilled employees. Addressing this talent gap is crucial for organizations aiming to remain competitive in this rapidly changing landscape.

### **Ethics and Responsibility in AI's Future**

As advocates for the ethical use of generative AI, we discuss the importance of navigating risks, including bias, factual inaccuracies, and intellectual property rights. A balanced approach with human oversight is essential to mitigate these risks and maximize potential.

### **A Catalyst for Global GDP Growth**

Generative AI is expected to significantly contribute to labor productivity and facilitate the transition to new job roles, leading to a more sustainable and inclusive economy. Achieving this requires cross-sector collaboration to ensure responsible and sustainable technological progress.

At GO MO, we are committed to helping our clients seamlessly integrate this technology into their operations. By choosing us, you are not just shaping the future—you are leading it. Let's transform together. Contact us to share your curious thoughts and hypotheses about generative AI and start optimizing today.

## **Why the Language of Search Just Changed — And What You Need to Know**

The vocabulary of search has undergone its most dramatic transformation in two decades. Terms that didn't exist 3 years ago — GEO, AEO, LLM-O, AI Overviews, RAG, zero-click — are now core to every digital marketing strategy. If you're still operating with a purely keyword-centric SEO mindset, you're optimizing for a search engine that is rapidly becoming secondary.

This glossary is the most comprehensive, up-to-date reference of AI search terminology available — covering everything from the foundational acronyms (GEO, AEO, LLMO) through to the technical infrastructure (RAG, passage indexing, AI crawlers) and the measurement frameworks that prove ROI. Whether you're briefing a client, onboarding a new team member, or building your own AI search strategy from scratch, this is the resource to bookmark.

### **The AI Search Shift: Key Numbers**
